body:
I'd like to propose that we renumber all of the ASVS to eliminate holes and to reset some of the chapters that have a great deal of new findings. To that end, I'd like for there to be a discussion as this will be a big change for some of our larger users. 

For example, we've had a suggestion that we group together like controls in each chapter, such as in Authentication:

2.0.x - Identity requirements
2.1.x - Password requirements
2.2.x - MFA requirements
2.3.x - Credential Recovery requirements 
2.4.x - ... 

3.1.x - Session management fundamentals
3.2.x - Federated session management
3.3.x - Serverless / client-side session management

4.1.x - Access control fundamentals
4.2.x - Model authz
4.3.x - Domain authz
4.4.x - Controller / Router authz
4.5.x - Presentation authz

5.1.x - Input validation fundamentals
5.2.x - Output encoding fundamentals
5.3.x - XSS requirements
5.4.x - SQLi requirements 
5.5.x - OS command requirements
5.6.x - XXE requirements
5.7.x - SSRF requirements

etc

@danielcuthbert @jmanico 

@eoftedal @sergicles @EnDe @thesp0nge @psiinon @dancornell @jeremylong @markdenihan @stuartgunter

I think that sounds like a good proposal. Once you've discussed with the project leads, it would be good to sketch out how you see the transition moving forward.

For example, will we have a separate PR for the changes to each chapter, introducing the subcategories and allowing for feedback / comments from ASVS users? Is there a date by which we need to finalise the changes, so this can be communicated to users? etc.

Stuart

There's no way around it for V2 - NIST 800-63 is so very different, the
redline would be complete.

It is important to keep a mapping, but I believe this might be better as a
chapter at the end to better allow folks to consume it electronically. This
is one of the most requested things is an XML or JSON version of the ASVS
that also has a complete mapping.to previous versions as well as other
standards, CWEs, etc.

Let me know what you think
